newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss Novartis shares ease in debut.
newsitem.headline: Swiss Novartis shares ease in debut.

text.p: The stock of Novartis, the world's second largest pharmaceutical company that was formed by merging Swiss rivals Ciba-Geigy and Sandoz, eased on their first day of trading Monday.
Novartis made its debut at 1,502 Swiss francs ($1,120) per registered share, then eased through the day before closing at 1,488 francs ($1,110).

This was a 0.4 percent decline from Friday's close in Sandoz, whose shares were swapped one to one for Novartis. One Novartis share is worth 1-1/15 Ciba shares, which ended at 1,595 francs on Friday (1,190).
Traders said the market, already dulled by very thin pre-Christmas volume, reacted with disappointment late in the day after no major buying of the shares appeared.
"People may have expected more on the first day of trading," one trader said.
Analysts said the price transition from Sandoz and Ciba to Novartis went much as expected with no sudden jumps because it had been planned and prepared for nine months.
"We were expecting a smooth transition like this," Jo Walton at Lehman Brothers said.

Many analysts agree with projections by Novartis of higher profits and lower costs in 1997 based on merger synergies and savings and expect the stock price to gain more strongly than the overall blue-chip Swiss Market Index next year.
Ciba and Sandoz have estimated the merger would save about two billion francs ($1.5 billion) over three years, including cutting the combined workforce by about 10 percent, or 12,000 jobs.
